- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean reversion; if price drops 2–4% from recent peak, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below prior low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 1–2% below true outcome for first 5 days.
- If sentiment is rising (increasing from 0.33 to 1.00) and price is rising, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven acceleration; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
